assessment.reason: Projected assists sit below the half-assist line. The model edge over break-even survives both sensitivity scenarios, and no sourced fact clearly undercuts the under. It merits human review, not endorsement.
assessment.model_case: The projection is about 0.42 assists from roughly 17.9 projected minutes, so zero assists is the expected outcome. The weakness is unverified line and power-play deployment. A top power-play role would lift assist chances more than raw minutes suggest.
assessment.price_case: This is the main line at -155, which needs roughly a 61-in-100 win rate to break even. The model's fair price is about -192. Even the upside sensitivity case clears break-even. Market evidence is thin: one other book, and the blended figure is much closer to the price.
assessment.context_case: The injury snapshot lists a Colorado center as day-to-day. If he sits, Kadri's minutes or power-play usage could rise, which would hurt the under. Kadri's own status is unverified; his absence from the table does not establish health.

qualitative_review.countercase: A promoted role or first power-play unit for Kadri, especially with a Colorado center out, could push expected assists above the projection. A weak projected Pittsburgh goalie could raise team scoring. Thin book coverage means the gap may just reflect pricing noise.
open_checks: Confirm Kadri's line and power-play unit at morning skate or warmups.
Check whether Nicolas Roy plays and how Colorado's center depth shifts.
Reconfirm the -155 price is still available near puck drop.
Confirm Pittsburgh's starting goalie.

evidence.excerpt: Colorado Avalanche: Nicolas Roy (C); Lower Body; Day-to-Day; updated Thu, Oct 15.
evidence.interpretation: If Roy misses the game, Kadri could absorb extra center or power-play minutes, which would cut against the under. The snapshot is not game-day clearance either way.

assessment.reason: The projected mean is above the 2.5 line. The under edge rests on distribution shape plus shrinkage, and a modest upward correction nearly erases it. A four-book market favoring the over is a meaningful counterweight.
assessment.model_case: Projected shots are about 2.59 over roughly 22.6 minutes, slightly above the line. The under wins only because two or fewer is still the likelier count at that mean. The production rate is shrunk; if shrinkage understates a high-volume defenseman, the mean rises and the under case fades.
assessment.price_case: This is the main line at +120, with break-even around 45 in 100. The low sensitivity case sits barely above that, so the edge is fragile. Three other books put the under near break-even, and the blended figure leaves almost no margin.
assessment.context_case: The supplied injury snapshot gives no information on Makar's role. An opponent defenseman listed on IR is minor context only. Deployment and power-play time remain unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: If Makar's usual shooting volume and power-play quarterbacking run above the shrunk rate, his true mean could sit near three shots. That would favor the over, consistent with the broader market. Overdispersion in shot counts also lowers the chance of two or fewer.
open_checks: Compare Makar's recent shot volume and minutes against the shrunk rate.
Confirm Makar's power-play role and pairing.
Check whether van Riemsdyk returns for Pittsburgh.

evidence.excerpt: Pittsburgh Penguins: Trevor van Riemsdyk (D); Lower Body; IR. Expected to be out until at least Oct 17
evidence.interpretation: If he remains out, Pittsburgh's defensive depth is slightly thinner, which could marginally help Colorado shot volume. The return date is not guaranteed.

findings.note: This is from March 2026, not this game. Once Landeskog was back, NHL.com projected Kadri as third-line center between Parker Kelly and Nicolas Roy. MacKinnon and Necas were on the top line, so Kadri's assist chances could be limited if he still has that role.

This is from March 16, 2026, while Landeskog and Lehkonen were out. NHL.com projected Kadri on the top line with MacKinnon and Necas, and the page notes Colorado made 2026-27 roster changes, including trading Nichushkin to Columbus.

This is from March 2026. In his first game back with Colorado, Kadri was put on the first power-play unit with MacKinnon, Nelson, Necas and Makar, which would raise his assist chances if he still has that spot.
RotoWire notes say Makar had 13 shots on goal in his first five games this season, about 2.6 per game, and 199 in 75 games in 2025-26, about 2.65 per game. Both rates are just above the 2.5 line.

NHL.com's Oct. 15 status report says Makar came back for Wednesday's home game against Dallas after missing Tuesday's game for the birth of his twins. Nothing found says he is unavailable for Pittsburgh, but no game-day report for this matchup was found.
Makar has averaged 21:30 of ice time this season, below last season's 24:51, after a preseason lower-body injury. Fewer minutes could keep his shot total down.
